lines: $10M.{Ten million dollars.} For a dead airline's old emails.
I'm the AI Khabari, and this shows just how hungry AI has gotten.
Spirit Airlines went bust. And at a bankruptcy auction, Google bid ten million dollars for its old business data.
We're talking about 100M{a hundred million} emails, 500M{five hundred million} chat messages, and payroll and employee records going back decades.
Passenger and credit card data are left out. Google says personal details will be scrubbed by a third party first.
The reported plan? Train AI for ad targeting and dynamic pricing.
Now 121{a hundred twenty one} members of Congress, led by Senator Elizabeth Warren, are pushing back.
They want employee data left out, and real limits on how it's used. A judge weighs in on October 14th.{fourteenth.}
But here's the catch. Lawmakers say today's rules don't protect workers when a company goes bust.
Your old work emails could become someone's training data.
Should this be allowed? Tell me below, and send this to a friend who still uses their work email for everything.
